newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, April 2.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italy said it would press ahead with plans to lead an international security force to troubled Albania despite mounting domestic pressure to reconsider the programme after the fatal sinking of a crowded refugee boat. Defence minister Beniamino Andreatta said the Italian-dominated force, expected to number some 5,000 men, could be deployed in the Balkan country by April 10. The Italian security force will avoid the southern city of Vlore (all).

* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party and the Green party said they opposed sending a multinational force to Albania, as it would be a mistake in the current conditions, and threatened to vote against the move in parliament (all).

* A report by the Treasury Ministry showed that Italy's cumulative public sector borrowing requirement was around 24.0 trillion lire at end-March 1997, compared with 46.324 trillion in the first quarter of 1996. Italian PSBR in March was 17.5 trillion lire, more than 3.0 trillion less than in March 1996 (all).
* Milan stock exchange fell 1.61 percent following the weakness of European bourses caused by Wall Street losses (all).

* The Treasury said it planned to place a third tranche of energy giant ENI on the stock market by the summer. The Treasury currently holds 69 percent of ENI and Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the state's holding will not fall below 51 percent (all).

* An agreement between information technology group Olivetti and France Telecom is reportedly near to conclusion. Industry minister Pier Luigi Bersani said he intends to provide fiscal incentives to information technology groups (Sole 24 Ore).

* Broadcasting group Mediaset will reportedly post a 445-450 billion lire net profit in 1996 from 454.6 in 1995. Mediaset is reportedly considering a rise in the dividend payout. The group board will meet tomorrow to present 1996 official results (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
